'''Mauro Picone''' (2 May 1885 – 11 April 1977) was an Italian [[mathematician]]. He is known for the [[Picone identity]], the [[Sturm-Picone comparison theorem]] and being the founder of the [[Istituto per le Applicazioni del Calcolo]], presently named after him, the first [[applied mathematics]] institute ever founded.<ref>See {{harv|Fichera|1995|pp=10–11}}, {{harv|Fichera|1999|p=297}}, {{harv|Benzi|2005|loc=p. 3 of the preprint version}} and the references cited in this latter one.</ref> He was also an outstanding teacher of [[mathematical analysis]]: some of the best Italian mathematicians were among his pupils.
[[File:picone1903.jpg|right|thumb|Mauro Picone in 1903]]

==Work==

===Research activity===
{{blockquote
|text= Attraverso le sue ricerche di analisi matematica, Mauro Picone ha contribuito notevolmente allo sviluppo della matematica del nostro secolo. Egli è stato inoltre un pioniere delle matematiche applicate.<ref>(English translation): "''Through his research in mathematical analysis, Mauro Picone contributed greatly to the development of mathematics of the present century. He was also a pioneer in applied mathematics''".</ref>
|sign= [[Radu Voinea]]
|source= {{harv|Voinea|1986|p=38}}.
}}

"''Mauro Picone and the Istituto Nazionale per le Applicazioni del Calcolo''" is a brief historical survey of Picone's role in the founding of the [[Istituto Nazionale per le Applicazioni del Calcolo]]: the Author is one of his pupils, former workers and then director of the institute. It was presented at the ''International congress in occasion of the celebration of the centenary of birth of Mauro Picone and Leonida Tonelli'' (held in [[Rome]] on May 6–9, 1985): an English translation of the title of the conference is:-''The work of Leonida Tonelli and his influence on scientific thinking in this century''.
